haiku-low.q1: MySQL first, in one transaction with the pending-row upsert; then Postgres safe-copy. If Postgres fails, the caller still gets success.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the id is not in that database's users_tombstones and the incoming version is higher than the existing row's version.
haiku-low.q3: Step 3 must be confirmed on every instance, and at least 1 minute must pass after that. Flag changes reach all instances within 30 s.
haiku-low.q4: Batches of at most 2,000 rows, read from the MySQL replica, and the loop pauses while replica lag exceeds 5 s.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: a clean comparer pass (0 mismatches) from step 5. Source of truth: reads at 100% for 3 days with the latest nightly comparer at 0 mismatches.
haiku-low.q6: A pending row (users_pg_pending in MySQL) committed with the change records it. The MySQL sweeper re-copies the user into Postgres, retrying until it succeeds.
haiku-low.q7: Copies and deletes take the same per-id lock, and the delete writes a tombstone; safe copy skips any id that is tombstoned.
haiku-low.q8: Table users_backfill_progress. Each batch's copy and cursor update share one Postgres transaction. Stops when no rows at or below target_max_id remain.
haiku-low.q9: The comparer scans both databases in 10,000-id chunks. Differences persisting after a 5 s primary recheck go to the pending table for sweeper repair.
haiku-low.q10: Writes freeze (503) and wait for confirmation plus 5 s, so no mixed writers. If not done by T0+60 s, revert to dual_mysql_primary.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns ids. Identity restarts at MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT value n, above all issued ids. On rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set to Postgres's next value.
haiku-low.q12: Each write is safe-copied to MySQL with its explicit id; the Postgres sweeper repairs misses. Rollback needs Postgres reachable; it ends at pg_only (step 10).

sonnet.q1: MySQL first: one MySQL transaction changes the user and upserts the users_pg_pending row, and commits. Then the row is safe-copied into Postgres (500 ms timeout). If the Postgres part fails or times out, the caller still sees success; the pending row stays and the MySQL sweeper repairs Postgres.
sonnet.q2: Only when the incoming version is higher than the existing row's version (and the id is not in Postgres's users_tombstones; if absent it is simply inserted).
sonnet.q3: Backfill starts at least 1 minute after dual_mysql_primary (step 3) is confirmed on every instance (so no mysql_only write can still commit and the replica holds all such writes). Instances can disagree for up to 30 s after a flag change.
sonnet.q4: It reads from the MySQL replica (not the primary, except one max(id) read at start), in batches of at most 2,000 rows, and waits whenever replica lag is above 5 s.
sonnet.q5: Reads move: backfill done and a full comparer pass reporting 0 mismatches. Source of truth moves: reads held at 100% for at least 3 days (each earlier level held at least 1 h within MySQL baseline for errors/p99) and the latest nightly comparer pass shows 0 mismatches; then pick a quiet time.
sonnet.q6: A row in the users_pg_pending table, kept in MySQL, upserted in the same transaction as the user change (so it survives a crash after commit). The MySQL sweeper (every 10 s, rows older than 5 s) re-reads the user from MySQL and safe-copies it to Postgres, then deletes the pending row if the token is unchanged.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: every delete removes the row and inserts the id into users_tombstones in the same transaction, in both databases. Safe copy skips ids in the target's tombstones, and copy and delete take a per-id lock so they cannot interleave.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres table users_backfill_progress (one row: last_copied_id, target_max_id). Each batch's safe-copy and the update of last_copied_id happen in one Postgres transaction, so they commit or roll back together. It stops at target_max_id (max id on the MySQL primary read at start); done when a read finds no rows at or below it.
sonnet.q9: The comparer, which walks both databases 10,000 ids at a time comparing id, version and a hash of other columns (reading MySQL from the replica, pausing if lag > 5 s). It re-checks each difference on the source-of-truth primary 5 s later; if still different it is a mismatch and the id is added to the pending table in the source-of-truth database, and the sweeper repairs it. Each pass reports its mismatch count.
sonnet.q10: Set write_mode to frozen (writes get retryable 503), wait until confirmed on all instances plus 5 s (write deadline), so no old-mode write can commit; then drain the pending table, restart the Postgres identity, and set dual_pg_primary. If sub-steps 2 to 5 are not done by T0 + 60 s, set dual_mysql_primary instead (nothing to undo, retry another day). Either way the last instance resumes writes by T0 + 90 s.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns new ids via its identity column. Before the switch, its identity is restarted at n, the MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT counter (above every id MySQL issued, including erased ones). On rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is set to the Postgres identity's next value so MySQL cannot reissue an id Postgres used.
sonnet.q12: Each write commits in Postgres with an upsert to users_mysql_pending, then is safe-copied into MySQL with its explicit id; the Postgres sweeper repairs failures and the nightly comparer sends mismatches to the pending table. Rollback: freeze writes and confirm plus 5 s, wait for users_mysql_pending to be empty, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT to Postgres's next identity value, then set dual_mysql_primary and read_from_pg = 0 (abort back to dual_pg_primary if not done by T0 + 60 s; writes resume by T0 + 90 s). Needs Postgres reachable. The option ends at the first pg_only write (step 10), after at least 14 days in step 9.
